title: Probing Interfacial Magnetic Anisotropy in \texorpdfstring{CoV$_{2}$O$_{4}$}{CoV2O4} using Spin Hall Magnetoresistance
authors: Sairam Ithineni, Krishna Jha, Aditya A. Wagh, Shwetha G. Bhat, Debashree Nayak, K. Senapati, P. S. Anil Kumar, D. Samal
abstract: Spin Hall magnetoresistance (SMR) has emerged as a powerful probe for investigating interfacial spin transport and magnetic anisotropy in complex oxide heterostructures. In this work, we investigate the interfacial magnetic anisotropy in Pt/CVO through angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements. Unlike the bulk-sensitive magnetic measurements on both strained CVO and Pt/CVO films, which exhibit a ferrimagnetic transition at $T_{C} \approx 150$ K accompanied by out-of-plane anisotropy that reorients toward in-plane anisotropy below 90 K, SMR reveals a distinct interfacial magnetic anisotropy. The rotational scans of the in-plane transverse SMR at 20 K exhibit substantial hysteresis about [100], while no hysteresis is observed along [110] and [1$\bar{1}$0], indicating a biaxial anisotropy with easy axes along [110] and [1$\bar{1}$0]. Furthermore, the absence of sharp discontinuities in both the in-plane longitudinal and transverse SMR, together with pronounced discontinuities near the in-plane [010] direction during out-of-plane rotation, strongly indicates the presence of in-plane anisotropy. This behavior persists up to 120 K. The discrepancy between the bulk-sensitive magnetic measurements and the SMR response suggests that the Pt/CVO interface retains a magnetic anisotropy distinct from the bulk, highlighting the interfacial sensitivity of SMR. Additionally, the spin mixing conductance is found to be of the order of $10^{14}$ $Ω^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-2}$, comparable to other oxide-based spintronic systems. These findings highlight the crucial role of interfacial effects in spin transport and establish Pt/CVO as a promising platform for spintronic applications.
summary: This study uses Spin Hall Magnetoresistance on $	ext{Pt}/	ext{CoV}_2	ext{O}_4$ thin films to investigate interfacial magnetic anisotropy. The SMR technique reveals a distinct biaxial in-plane easy axis at the interface, contradicting bulk measurements that suggest out-of-plane behavior. This highlights SMR's superior sensitivity for probing surface spin transport and establishes the material as a promising spintronic platform.
main_problem: The study investigates interfacial magnetic anisotropy in $	ext{CoV}_2	ext{O}_4$ ($	ext{CVO}$) thin films using Spin Hall Magnetoresistance (SMR) to distinguish surface effects from bulk behavior.
main_result: SMR measurements reveal a distinct biaxial in-plane magnetic anisotropy for the $	ext{Pt}/	ext{CVO}$ interface, which contrasts with the bulk material's tendency toward out-of-plane anisotropy at higher temperatures.
method: The research employs angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements (SMR) on epitaxial thin-film heterostructures ($	ext{Pt}/	ext{CVO}$) and compares these results against standard DC magnetization measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Pt}/	ext{CoV}_2	ext{O}_4/	ext{STO}(001)$ heterostructure. The analysis relies on modeling magnetotransport phenomena using SMR theory, which probes spin current accumulation at the interface.
key_observables: Angle-dependent transverse and longitudinal resistivity ($ho_{xy}, ho_{xx}$), hysteresis loops in SMR scans, and the estimated spin mixing conductance ($G_{	ext{mix}}$).
important_parameters: Temperature (down to 20 K), magnetic field strength (up to 3.5 kOe), and material parameters like the spin Hall angle of Pt.
main_assumptions: The SMR response is assumed to be highly sensitive to, and primarily reflect, the interfacial magnetic anisotropy rather than the bulk properties of $	ext{CVO}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural confirmation via XRD, temperature-dependent magnetization curves (ZFC/FC), and angular dependence plots ($ho_{xy}$ vs. angle) showing characteristic anisotropic modulations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the background on SMR as a probe for interfacial magnetism, presents experimental measurements comparing bulk magnetic data with SMR results, analyzes the directional dependence of the magnetotransport signal to deduce anisotropy type (biaxial in-plane), and concludes by quantifying the interface quality via spin conductance.
why_interesting: The work provides an excellent example of using transport measurements (SMR) to isolate and characterize subtle interfacial magnetic phenomena that are masked or misrepresented by bulk magnetization techniques, which is a key concept in modern spintronics research relevant to correlated oxides.

Figure 1(b) shows the θ–2θ scan of representative bare CoV2O4 (26 nm) and Pt (6 nm)/CoV2O4 (26 nm) thin films. The (001) diffraction peaks corre- sponding to the CVO layer are clearly observed in both samples, indicating oriented growth, while the Pt/CVO sample exhibits an additional peak aris- ing from the Pt overlayer. No impurity phases are detected, confirming that the crystallographic struc- ture of CVO remains preserved after Pt deposition.

Figure 2(a) shows the temperature-dependent magnetisation measured under zero-field-cooled (ZFC) and field-cooled (FC) conditions in an applied field of 100 Oe over the temperature range 5 to 300 K, with the magnetic field applied along the in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OP) directions of CVO/STO (001). Consistent with previous reports, the system undergoes a paramagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transi- tion near ∼150 K (Tc)[31, 36].
